evidence: Child 734d allowlist: 'The single-ticket MCP tool set mirrors the CLI allowlist: `show_ticket`, ... `archive_ticket`, `check_ac`.'
Child 734d Scope: 'src/rebar/_mcp_models.py — add `cross_session_warning: str | None = None` to `WriteAckOut` and `TicketStateOut`.' (no `GateResultOut`)
Codebase: `check_ac` MCP handler returns `GateResultOut` (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:406), which is neither WriteAckOut nor TicketStateOut
findings.finding: Child 734d lists `check_ac` in its single-ticket MCP allowlist that should carry `cross_session_warning`, but its Approach/Scope only add the field to `WriteAckOut` and `TicketStateOut`; the `check_ac` handler returns `GateResultOut` (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:406), which is never given the field — so `check_ac` cannot actually carry the warning as the allowlist implies.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `cross_session_warning: str | None = None` to `GateResultOut` and populate it in the `check_ac` handler, or drop `check_ac` from 734d's allowlist to match the CLI/MCP/library reconciliation.

evidence: CLI child 5d55: allowlist 'covers ... `show`, `comment`, `edit`, `transition`, `reopen`, `tag`, `untag`, `set-file-impact`, `declare-no-file-impact`, `deps`, `archive`, `check-ac`, `clarity-check`, `link`, `unlink`'

Library child 3d8a: 'the read `show_ticket` ... and `deps`; the writes transition / reopen ... comment, edit, tag, untag, set_file_impact, declare_no_file_impact, link ... unlink ... archive' — no `check_ac`, no `clarity_check`
MCP child 734d: 'mirrors the CLI allowlist: `show_ticket`, `comment_ticket`, ... `archive_ticket`, `check_ac`' — no `ticket_deps`, no `clarity_check`

Codebase confirms all three exist per surface: `rebar.deps`/`rebar.check_ac`/`rebar.clarity_check` (src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:172, src/rebar/_lib_gates.py:35/61); MCP `ticket_deps`/`clarity_check`/`check_ac` (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:313/400/406); CLI `clarity-check` (src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:246)
findings.finding: The three surface children each state their single-ticket allowlist 'mirrors' the others, but the enumerated allowlists diverge: `deps`/`ticket_deps` is included on CLI (5d55) and library (3d8a) but absent from MCP (734d); `check_ac`/`check-ac` is included on CLI (5d55) and MCP (734d) but absent from library (3d8a); `clarity-check`/`clarity_check` is included on CLI (5d55) but absent from both MCP and library.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the canonical single-ticket allowlist once (e.g. in the detector story 0804 or the parent), enumerate exactly which single-ticket ops warn, and have each surface child reference that one list rather than restating a divergent set.

evidence: 5d55 Approach: 'add the stderr emit at each allowlisted command's resolved-id point (which may be require_id ... or a command's own id-resolution arm)' and 'the frozenset membership check - not a require_id call - is what excludes bulk commands ... not a single shared id-resolution helper.'
3d8a Surface layering: 'execute() runs _maybe_warn_cross_session (the allowlist single source) and handler dispatch inside suppress_cross_session_warning()'
The two children disagree on whether the CLI advisory is emitted at each command's own id-resolution arm (5d55) or by one centralized name-keyed helper in execute() (3d8a).
findings.finding: Children 5d55 and 3d8a describe two incompatible CLI emit architectures for the same seam. 5d55's Approach mandates a PER-COMMAND resolved-id insertion and explicitly states it is 'not a single shared id-resolution helper', while 3d8a describes a single centralized helper (_maybe_warn_cross_session, 'the allowlist single source') run inside execute().
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt one architecture in both children: since 3d8a's dedup requires a single wrap point, revise 5d55's Approach to specify a single centralized name-keyed helper at the dispatch layer (e.g. _maybe_warn_cross_session in _cli/_execute.py) rather than per-command resolved-id insertions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the explicit ordering that the library-surface child (3d8a) must land AFTER the CLI (5d55) and MCP (734d) children, and reconcile the 'non-overlapping seam' claim with 3d8a editing _cli/_execute.py and mcp_server.py.
evidence: Parent decomposition: 'Each child owns a distinct, non-overlapping seam (reducer state, pure detector+config, CLI rendering, MCP model/schema, library warnings channel).'
Parent decomposition declares CLI/MCP/library children each only 'Depends on the detector' — no inter-sibling dependency stated.

Library child Scope: 'src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py — hold suppress_cross_session_warning() across detection + dispatch so the library never doubles the CLI WARN: line.' and 'src/rebar/mcp_server.py — build_server() wraps read/write tool registration with the suppress_library_double_advisory proxy.'
Library child dedup AC asserts against a CLI test file: 'a warning CLI command (e.g. link) writes exactly one WARN: line ... (test_cross_session_cli.py count(...) == 1).'
findings.finding: The library child owns cross-cutting suppression edits to the CLI and MCP surface files, creating a hidden inter-sibling dependency and scope overlap that contradicts the parent's 'distinct, non-overlapping seam' decomposition and its 'each depends only on the detector' ordering.
scenarios: Landing order: if the library child lands before the CLI/MCP children register their advisories, the suppression wraps nothing; if the CLI/MCP children land first, they double the advisory until the library child lands.
Two children editing src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py (CLI child adds the emit; library child adds the suppress wrapper) collide on the same seam.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the parent decomposition (and in 3d8a) that dedup/suppression is a cross-surface concern owned by the library child which depends on and must sequence after the CLI and MCP children; or relocate the CLI/MCP suppression wrapping into their respective surface children so each surface owns its own dedup.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare in the CLI child (5d55) that its single-WARN behavior depends on the library child's suppress_cross_session_warning() wrapper (or make 5d55 own its own suppression), and add the dependency edge.
evidence: CLI child Scope covers only 'The CLI dispatch layer under src/rebar/_cli/ — define the allowlist frozenset ... and add the stderr emit' and 'docs/user-guide.md' — no mention of the library CrossSessionWarning doubling or its suppression.
CLI child depends line: 'Depends on the detector ... and on the reducer clearing.' — the library child is not named as a dependency.
Library child asserts the CLI single-emit invariant: 'a warning CLI command (e.g. link) writes exactly one WARN: line, not doubled by the library channel.'

Repo confirmation: src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py wraps _maybe_warn_cross_session + _invoke in suppress_cross_session_warning(), and CLI handlers dispatch to instrumented library mutators that would otherwise emit CrossSessionWarning.
findings.finding: The CLI child's spec relies on suppression it neither owns nor mentions: its behavior (a single WARN line) is only correct once the library channel is suppressed, but that suppression is specified in the library child, leaving a dependency gap in the CLI child.
scenarios: A CLI command like `rebar comment <id>` dispatches to the instrumented rebar.comment(); absent the library child's suppress wrapper the process both writes WARN: to stderr and emits a stdlib CrossSessionWarning.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the suppression-wrapper edit to the CLI child's Scope and name library-channel suppression as its responsibility, or explicitly declare the CLI child depends on the library child for dedup.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare the MCP child (734d) dependency on the library child's suppress_library_double_advisory proxy (or have 734d own MCP-side library suppression), and record the required landing order.
evidence: MCP child Approach: single-ticket handlers call 'cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, ...)' then perform 'rebar.<op>(...)' — the library op it invokes is the one the library child (3d8a) instruments to emit CrossSessionWarning.
MCP child Scope and depends line name only the detector and reducer clearing; no mention of the library-channel double emission or its suppression.
Library child Scope: 'src/rebar/mcp_server.py — build_server() wraps read/write tool registration with the suppress_library_double_advisory proxy (scoped per-handler suppression; no global filter).'
Repo confirmation: _mcp_writes.py:290-306 transition_ticket calls _cross_session(ticket_id) AND rebar.transition(...) (instrumented).
findings.finding: The MCP child computes its own warning AND dispatches to instrumented library mutators, so without the library child's suppress_library_double_advisory proxy the MCP process double-emits (response field plus stdlib CrossSessionWarning); this coupling/dependency is unstated in the MCP child.
scenarios: An MCP write tool (e.g. comment_ticket / transition_ticket) run as a different session would populate cross_session_warning in the response and, absent the library child's proxy, also raise a stdlib CrossSessionWarning inside the server process (leaking to unrelated import-rebar callers sharing the process).
findings.suggested_fix: Name the library-double-advisory suppression as an explicit dependency of the MCP child, or move the per-handler suppression into the MCP child so the MCP surface owns its own dedup end to end.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether multi-ticket-by-id operations count as single-ticket (warn per held id) or as bulk (silent), so each surface story classifies operations consistently.
evidence: 'Fires only on single-ticket-targeted operations (single-ticket reads like show plus single-ticket mutations)'
bulk reads enumerated as 'list / search / ready / next-batch' but multi-id-by-argument operations not addressed
findings.finding: The set of 'single-ticket-targeted operations' is given by example ('comment, edit, tag, transition, or even just show') rather than an enumerated boundary; commands that target multiple tickets by explicit id (e.g. a batch transition or multi-id show) are not classified as single-ticket or bulk, leaving the warn/no-warn decision ambiguous for those.
findings.location: Context/Problem + AC line 3 ('surfaced for single-ticket-targeted operations ... never on bulk reads')
scenarios: An operation accepting several ticket ids where one is held by another session — implementer must decide whether to warn per-id, once, or not at all
findings.suggested_fix: Add a decision: an operation targeting >1 ticket id is treated as bulk (silent); only operations with exactly one target ticket warn.
